head.citation-title: Microstructure and water absorption of chloride-containing hardened cement pastes under accelerated carbonation condition
head.abstracts: © 2025The microstructure and water absorption properties are critical factors that influence the durability of concrete. And the utilization of marine resources such as seawater and sea sand are of great significance to the sustainable development of concrete. This study evaluates the microstructure and capillary water absorption of chloride-containing cement pastes under accelerated carbonation condition. The results indicate that incorporating 0.5–2 % chloride ions reduces the calcium carbonate produced by carbonation, thereby enhancing the carbonation resistance of the cement pastes. Chloride salts can refine the pore composition of hardened cement paste and mitigate the coarsening of pore structures caused by carbonation. Notably, the incorporation of sodium chloride markedly enhances the water retention capacity, resulting in an increase in initial water content by 138.9–364.8 %. While carbonation leads to a decrease in water retention capacity and accelerates moisture transport of cement paste. The initial water content and pore composition were found to be the primary factors influencing the water absorption of hardened cement pastes. The addition of chloride noticeably reduced the water absorption rate and the cumulative water absorption. Instead, the water absorption values increased by 13.2–292.3 % under accelerated carbonation condition. The water absorption patterns observed using the Low-Field NMR method matched with those obtained by the weighing method. Moreover, LF NMR offers a distinctive advantage by effectively monitoring water distribution and transport throughout the capillary absorption process.

coredata.dc:description: The microstructure and water absorption properties are critical factors that influence the durability of concrete. And the utilization of marine resources such as seawater and sea sand are of great significance to the sustainable development of concrete. This study evaluates the microstructure and capillary water absorption of chloride-containing cement pastes under accelerated carbonation condition. The results indicate that incorporating 0.5–2 % chloride ions reduces the calcium carbonate produced by carbonation, thereby enhancing the carbonation resistance of the cement pastes. Chloride salts can refine the pore composition of hardened cement paste and mitigate the coarsening of pore structures caused by carbonation. Notably, the incorporation of sodium chloride markedly enhances the water retention capacity, resulting in an increase in initial water content by 138.9–364.8 %. While carbonation leads to a decrease in water retention capacity and accelerates moisture transport of cement paste. The initial water content and pore composition were found to be the primary factors influencing the water absorption of hardened cement pastes. The addition of chloride noticeably reduced the water absorption rate and the cumulative water absorption. Instead, the water absorption values increased by 13.2–292.3 % under accelerated carbonation condition. The water absorption patterns observed using the Low-Field NMR method matched with those obtained by the weighing method. Moreover, LF NMR offers a distinctive advantage by effectively monitoring water distribution and transport throughout the capillary absorption process.
coredata.dc:title: Microstructure and water absorption of chloride-containing hardened cement pastes under accelerated carbonation condition
